newsitem.title: POLAND: Shell to invest $60 mln in Poland in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Shell to invest $60 mln in Poland in 1997.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group will invest $60 million in Poland next year, its managing director Steve Miller said.
Miller, who was due on Thursday to open a $6 million Shell liquid petroleum gas (lpg) filling plant in Lodz, its fourth in Poland, did not specify targets for the investment.

"Our investment in Poland next year will be equal to all the money invested in Poland over the last four years -- and this is before the privatisation opportunities we are looking forward to working on with the ministries and industry," Miller told a reception in Warsaw's royal palace.

Miller added it was hard to say what investments Shell would make in Poland, where the economy was growing fast and demand for fuel was rising 4-6 percent a year, as opportunities were so wide, including chemicals and exploration.
"You can pick any business and it is going to be attractive," said Miller, who on Wednesday met Polish government and oil industry officials.
Shell officials have said they are potentially interested in a share of the privatisation of Polish refineries, but will only decide when details of the process become clear.

In May, Poland set up a Nafta Polska SA holding company, grouping its state refineries and largest fuel distribution network as a step towards making the sector competitive before protective duties on imports are lifted around the year 2000.

Miller's visit to Poland coincides with that of European Commissioner Hans van den Broek, who was arriving in Poland on Thursday for tough talks on what the EU sees as delays in deregulating Poland's closely protected oil industry.
Nick Brooks, director of operating company Shell Polska Ltd, told Reuters that the company would not be involved in the talks, as it could present its views directly.
"There is a strong desire to see a clear path towards deregulation and privatisation and to see a clear timetable for steps that have been discussed over the past year," he said.

Shell has 25 petrol stations and a further 10 are to open by the end of the year -- although it has yet to turn a profit -- showing it does not plan to follow Amoco Corp's decision this month to sell its retail petrol stations in the country.
Shell has concessions in potential gas fields in western Poland which would be operated by Exxon.
Among other areas, the company is heavily involved in chemicals and Poland is an approved centre for making Shell car care products as well as a market for its imported lubricants.
Shell has a $40 million tanker being built in the Szczecin shipyard, also on the Baltic coast.
